annotationRationale: The method reduces the process to two states, finds the same transition probability from each, and combines the cases by total probability. Independence justifies multiplying the required choices.
sourceMethod: Followed the official two-state argument, clarifying why a player cannot finish with all three dollars and making the final total-probability step explicit.

review.mathCheck: Total money remains 3, and no round can end with one player holding all 3. From (1,1,1), two of eight equally likely choices return to equality; from any permutation of (2,1,0), one of four does. Both probabilities are 1/4, so the probability after round 2019 is 1/4, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA 10B solution 22 on page 10. It strengthens the exclusion of a three-dollar holder and explicitly writes the final total-probability calculation.
review.annotationCheck: The state reduction and transition probabilities are justified. Their equality makes the unknown distribution before round 2019 irrelevant, so no preceding-round computation is missing.
